# peek-app-utilities

> Dependency-light **async** Python library wrapping the Peek "backoffice" API
> (plus the CNG and ACME backoffice APIs). Callers only touch
> `PeekAccessService`, the per-resource services it hands out, and clean
> dataclass models — never raw GraphQL. Python ≥ 3.11; runtime dependencies:
> `httpx`, `PyJWT`. It is the Python port of `@peektravel/app-utilities` and
> ships the **same version number**, resources, models, and behaviour; names
> are the TypeScript ones in `snake_case` (`getById` → `get_by_id`,
> `customerName` → `customer_name`), class names unchanged.

The authoritative, always-in-sync contract is the typed source
(`peek_app_utilities` ships `py.typed`; every public class and method has a
docstring) — read it via go-to-definition. This file is a map; the docstrings
and `README.md` (also shipped) have full detail and examples.

## Entry point

Construct one `PeekAccessService` per install, then call `get_<resource>_service()`
accessors (each memoized, bound to a shared authenticated transport that mints
and caches a short-lived JWT). Everything that does I/O is `async def`. Use the
service as an async context manager (or `await peek.aclose()`) to close the HTTP
client it owns; a caller-supplied `http_client` is never closed.

```python
from peek_app_utilities import PeekAccessService, PeekAccessServiceConfig

async with PeekAccessService(PeekAccessServiceConfig(
    install_id=install_id,   # JWT subject
    jwt_secret=jwt_secret,   # HMAC secret signing the JWT
    issuer=issuer,           # app name (JWT issuer)
    api_url=api_url,         # the install webhook's api_url — the base API URL; each service appends its own slug
    # optional: gateway_key, token_ttl_seconds, token_refresh_leeway_seconds,
    # retry_delays_ms, logger, http_client, item_options_page_size,
    # access_options=AccessOptions(full_customer_access=False)  # default — see "Access options / PII"
)) as peek:
    products = await peek.get_product_service().get_all_products()
```

Targeting an install by URL: pass the install webhook's `api_url` as the config
`api_url`. It is the install's **base API URL**; each service class appends its own
backoffice slug (e.g. `peek_backoffice_api-v1`, from a small per-platform endpoint
lookup) when it calls — so a Peek call goes to `<base>/peek_backoffice_api-v1`
and a CNG/ACME call to `<base>/<slug>/<path>`. If the URL you pass already
carries this platform's slug (dashes or underscores interchangeable) it is
**stripped** back to the base; a URL carrying a *different* platform's slug is
**rejected** (constructor raises `ValueError`). No app-id segment is inserted
(`app_id` is unused). `create_access_service_for_install(install, InstallAccessConfig(...))`
builds the right service for `install.platform` (`peek`/`cng`/`acme`) wired to
`install.api_url` in one call (raises `ValueError` on unknown/`None` platform).
`app_id` + `base_url` + `mode` (and the hardcoded gateway default) are
**deprecated** — they reconstruct the URL with a compiled-in default that can't
be right for every install; the fallbacks will be removed and a URL will become
**required**.

## Access options / PII — `full_customer_access`

**The most commonly-misunderstood option in this package. Read this before
debugging "why is `customer_name` None?" or "why did `make_payment` raise?".**

Every access service takes `access_options: AccessOptions | None`
(`AccessOptions(full_customer_access: bool | None = None)`). It is passed
**once at construction**, not per call, and applies to every service that access
service hands out.

```python
peek = PeekAccessService(PeekAccessServiceConfig(
    install_id=install_id, jwt_secret=jwt_secret, issuer=issuer, api_url=api_url,
    access_options=AccessOptions(full_customer_access=True),  # opt in to PII + payment ops
))
```

- **Default is `False` (PII off).** Omitting `access_options`, passing
  `AccessOptions()`, or passing `None` are all identical to
  `AccessOptions(full_customer_access=False)`.
- There is **no per-call override** by design — an install either has customer-
  data entitlement or it doesn't. Need both modes? Construct two access services.
- Consumed by `BookingService` and `ReviewService`; `parse_waiver_webhook(body,
  options=None)` takes the same object directly. `CngAccessService` /
  `AcmeAccessService` accept the field but have no PII surface (inert).

### With `full_customer_access=False` (default) — two distinct effects

**1. PII is never requested.** Filtering happens in the query selection, so the
data never leaves the API; the fields simply arrive as `None`/empty in the
clean models. There is no error and no warning — a missing name looks exactly
like a customer who didn't provide one.

| Surface | Redacted (→ `None`/empty) | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Booking | primary-guest `customer_name`/`customer_email`/`customer_phone`; per-guest identity (name, country, DOB, email, phone, postal code, `is_gdpr`, custom `metadata` field responses) — guests keep only ids + participation/opt-in flags; booking- and ticket-level `custom_question_answers` / `custom_guest_question_answers`; the customer `portal_url`; the `name`/`email`/`date_of_birth` of a `guest`-kind `MetaData` value | notes, `custom_status`, Peek Pro operator deep link, money/price breakdown, resources, timeslot + structural ids |
| Review | reviewer `customer_name` / `customer_email` | comment, rating, dates, credited guides |
| Waiver webhook | participant `guest_name` (→ `None`), signed-document `file_url` (→ `""`) — redacted at parse time; the payload is fixed, so there is no selection to trim | template/booking ids, timestamps, guardian + opt-in flags |

**2. Payment & booking-modification operations are disabled.** These raise
`PiiAccessDisabledError` (exported; `.operation` names the blocked method in
snake_case) **before any network call**:

`get_payments_on_file`, `make_payment`, `refund`, `create_invoice_link`,
`add_addon`, `remove_addon`.

Still available without the flag: `create` (**including `mark_as_paid`**),
`get_by_id`, `get_guests`, `search_by_time_range`, `search_by_timeslot`,
`list_addons`, `cancel`, `append_note`, `set_checkin_status`,
`update_custom_status`, `get_meta_data`, the `set_meta_data_*` setters, and
every other resource service.

### Choosing a value

Leave it `False` for operations/logistics tooling (manifests, check-in, guide
assignment, notes, availability) — that surface is fully functional without PII.
Set it `True` only when the app genuinely needs to contact customers or move
money, and only when the install is entitled to that data; the API is the final
authority and may still reject the request.

## Resources (accessor → methods)

All methods are `async`; inputs are keyword-only frozen dataclasses exported
from the package root.

- `get_product_service()` — `get_all_products()` (flat list of activities +
  add-ons; add-ons have `type == ADD_ON_PRODUCT_TYPE`), `get_all_activities()`
  (`ACTIVITY_PRODUCT_TYPE` only), `get_all_rentals()` (`RENTAL_PRODUCT_TYPE`
  only), `get_all_addons()`. `Product.currency` carries the activity's ISO
  currency (empty for add-ons). Activities also expose the catalog fields
  `image_url`, `description`, and `meeting_location`
  (`ProductMeetingLocation(summary, address, url)`) — all nullable, and
  `meeting_location` is `None` when Peek reports no location detail (always
  `None` for add-ons). Each `Product.tickets[]` entry (`ProductTicket`) carries
  `min_price`/`max_price` (`PricingMoney | None`, `None` for add-ons and when
  Peek reports no range); every `PricingMoney` read back includes a
  `display_price` string (e.g. `"$50.00"`).
  `get_custom_questions(product_id)` returns an activity's operator-configured
  custom questions as `list[CustomQuestion]` — each with `id`, `order`,
  `is_required`, `question_text`, `hint_text`, `question_type`
  (`CHECK_BOX`/`TEXT`/`LOCATION`/`SELECT_ONE`/…), `internal_label`,
  `per_guest`, `default_value`, and `options: list[CustomQuestionOption]`
  (`id`, `order`, `value`; empty for free-text/checkbox questions). Question
  definitions, not answers — no PII. Raises `ValueError` on a blank id;
  returns `[]` for an unknown activity.
- `get_account_user_service()` — `get_all()` (active users only),
  `get_by_id(user_id)` → `AccountUser | None`
- `get_resource_pool_service()` — `get_all(mode=None)` (`ResourcePoolMode`
  `"ACTIVITY"`/`"ALL"`, default `"ALL"`)
- `get_timeslot_service()` — `get_for_day(product_id, date, filter=None)`
  (`TimeslotFilter` `"all"`/`"withBookings"`/`"withoutBookings"`),
  `get_by_id(timeslot_id)` → `Timeslot | None`,
  `set_availability(timeslot_id, status)`, `set_notes(timeslot_id, manifest_notes)`
  → `UpdateTimeslotResult`, `assign_guide(GuideAssignment(timeslot_ids,
  guide_ids, action))` → `AssignGuideResult` (guides matched by pool id,
  account-user id, or name; `action` is `"assign"`/`"unassign"`)
- `get_reseller_service()` — `get_all_channels(agents_per_channel=None)` (default 10)
- `get_promo_code_service()` — `get_all()`, `create(CreatePromoCodeInput)` →
  `CreatedPromoCode`
- `get_pricing_service()` — `create_engine(CreateEngineInput)`,
  `update_engine(UpdateEngineInput)`, `delete_engine(engine_id)` (idempotent),
  `upsert_overrides(UpsertOverridesInput)`, `clear_overrides(ClearOverridesInput)`.
  Primitives-only: caller builds the `UpsertOverridesInput` (segmentation,
  override `order`, `spots_taken` bounds are the caller's job); service sends it
  as-is and returns the resolved `activity_contexts`. The override variant
  classes (`FixedResourceOptionOverride`, `PercentageResourceOptionOverride`,
  `SpotsTakenFilter`/`SpotsTakenBounds`, `StartTimeRangeFilter`) live in
  `peek_app_utilities.models.peek.pricing`. Guide: `docs/external/pricing-api.md`.
- `get_daily_note_service()` — `get_today()` → `DailyNote | None`, `update(note)`
- `get_availability_service()` — `get_availability_times(AvailabilityTimesQuery(
  activity_id, date, resource_option_quantities))` → `list[AvailabilityTime]`
  (each with `id`, `time`, `from_`, `end`, `duration`, `status`, `availability`)
- `get_membership_service()` — `get_all()`, `purchase(MembershipPurchaseInput)`
  → `PurchasedMembership`
- `get_booking_service(integrator=None)` — `get_by_id(id, options: BookingReadOptions
  | None)` → `Booking | None`, `search_by_time_range(BookingTimeRangeSearch)`,
  `search_by_timeslot(timeslot_id, options=None)`, `get_guests(id)` → `list[Guest]`,
  `get_meta_data(id)` → `list[MetaData]` (booking custom-field responses, `[]` when
  not found; each `MetaData` carries a typed `value: MetaDataValue | None`
  discriminated union keyed by `kind` plus a display-safe `display_value` string
  on the `MetaData` itself (the `html` value's is HTML-escaped); returns only
  fields whose slug starts with `integrators:<integrator>:`, that prefix
  stripped). The `integrator` arg on the accessor scopes `get_meta_data` —
  **do not set it** unless Peek engineering created a custom integrator id for
  this integration.
  Eight metadata setters (fixed field name, caller supplies the value;
  integrator-scoped; return `SetMetaDataResult(success, booking_id, message)`;
  not PII-gated): `set_meta_data_guest(id, guests: Sequence[SetMetaDataGuestInput])`
  (name+email required), `set_meta_data_attachment(id, attachments:
  Sequence[SetMetaDataAttachmentInput])` (name+attachment_url required),
  `set_meta_data_manifest_url(id, url)`, `set_meta_data_reservation_id(id,
  reservation_id)`, `set_meta_data_booking_status(id, status)`,
  `set_meta_data_assigned_product(id, product_name)`,
  `set_meta_data_assigned_employee(id, employee_name)`,
  `set_meta_data_insurance_purchased(id, insurance_purchased: bool)`.
  `get_payments_on_file(id)` → `BookingPaymentsOnFile | None`,
  `append_note(id, note, mode="append")` (`NoteMode` `"append"`/`"overwrite"`)
  → `Booking | None`, `set_checkin_status(id, checked_in: bool)` → `Booking | None`,
  `update_custom_status(id, custom_status)` → `bool` (sets the operator custom
  status; not PII-gated), `cancel(id, notes="Canceled")` → `CancelBookingResult`,
  `make_payment(MakePaymentInput)` → `MakePaymentResult`, `refund(RefundInput)` →
  `RefundResult`, `create_invoice_link(id)` → `InvoiceLinkResult`,
  `list_addons(id)` → `BookingAddons`, `add_addon(id, AddAddonInput(addon_option_id,
  quantity))` and `remove_addon(id, AddAddonInput(...))` → `BookingAddonsMutationResult`,
  `create(CreateBookingInput)` → `CreatedBooking` (optional `list_price` — total
  booking price string, commas allowed; split evenly across tickets with the
  remainder cent on the last, sent per ticket in the activity currency, fallback
  USD)
- `get_review_service()` — `get_reviews(product_id, review_count=50, review_offset=0)`
  (single newest-first page of `Review`s, count 1–50, offset ≥ 0);
  `get_all_review_summaries()` → `list[ProductReviewSummary]` (one per activity:
  `avg_rating` — decimal, `None` when no ratings — plus `count_total` and per-star
  `count_one_star`…`count_five_star`). No PII; unaffected by `full_customer_access`.

Access-level: `verify_peek_auth_token(token)` → `PeekAuthTokenClaims(install_id,
display_version, user: PeekAuthTokenUser | None)`; `aclose()`; `async with`.

## Sibling accessors (CNG, ACME)

Two brand-parallel accessors sit alongside `PeekAccessService` and share the same
auth/transport plumbing. Both are deliberately minimal today (products only).
Construct one per install, same config shape **minus the Peek-only fields**
(`CngAccessServiceConfig` / `AcmeAccessServiceConfig` are aliases of
`BaseAccessServiceConfig`: `install_id`, `jwt_secret`, `issuer`, `api_url`, …).
With `api_url` set, it is the base API URL and the product service appends its
backoffice slug (`cng_backoffice_api-v1` / `acme_backoffice_api-v1`) and the
path; the deprecated `base_url`/`app_id` fall back to the app-registry default
(`<base_url>/<app_id>` as the base). `create_access_service_for_install` routes
`platform` `"cng"`/`"acme"` to these. Both support `aclose()` / `async with`.

- `CngAccessService` — `get_product_service().get_all_activities()` →
  `list[Activity]` (`Activity`/`ActivityTicket` models). Only
  `product_id`/`name`/`color` are populated: `type` is always `"ACTIVITY"` and
  `tickets` is always empty (CNG's products endpoint exposes neither). Only
  active products are returned. Errors surface as `CngApiError`, except HTTP
  403 — a missing app permission — which surfaces as `CngPermissionError`
  (`.permissions` lists the permission names, e.g. `["products:read"]`; logged
  at `warn`, meant to be caught and shown to the operator).
- `AcmeAccessService` — `get_product_service().get_all_activities()` →
  `list[AcmeActivity]` (`AcmeActivity`/`AcmeActivityTicket` models; published
  templates only). Errors surface as `AcmeApiError`.

All are exported from the package root `peek_app_utilities`; paths and raw
response shapes stay internal.

## Input conventions (enforced in the service layer; violations raise `ValueError`)

- Booking ids must be `b_…` (lowercase db id) or `B-…` (uppercase display id);
  they are normalized (lowercased, `-`→`_`) so `B-ABC123` == `b_abc123`. Order
  ids likewise `o_…`/`O-…`. Mixed forms are rejected.
- Quantities: positive-integer strings (`"1"`, `"2"`).
- Currency: 3-letter uppercase ISO (`"USD"`). Amounts: numeric strings (`"25.00"`).
- Payment source ids: `ps_…` or `cash/cash` | `custom/other` | `custom/voucher`.
  Payment ids (refunds): `pmt_…`.
- Idempotency key required on `make_payment`, `refund`, `create(... mark_as_paid=True)`.
- `create()` uses pre-resolved ids for product/ticket/time (resolve via product
  + availability services); no free-text matching there. The one exception is
  `CreateBookingInput.custom_question_answers: list[CustomQuestionAnswerInput] | None`
  (`question_id_or_text`, `value`): when supplied, the activity's custom
  questions are fetched and each answer is matched (id or lenient text) and
  validated by type (checkbox `yes/no/true/false`; text verbatim;
  select-one/location by option id or lenient label) before the quote is made —
  an unmatched/ambiguous question or option, or an invalid checkbox value,
  fails creation up front. Per-guest questions are not yet supported (answering
  one fails creation). `require_required_questions: bool | None` (default
  `False`) additionally enforces that every required (non-per-guest) custom
  question is answered — validation runs even when `custom_question_answers`
  is empty/omitted. `accept_all_custom_question_ids: bool | None` (default
  `False`) relaxes the id check: a `cq_…` id not in the activity's question list
  is accepted as a plain text answer instead of failing creation (by-name
  answers still must match). When every answer is by id (and no required check
  runs) the questions fetch is skipped entirely.

## Errors

- Every package error derives from `AppUtilitiesError`:
  `AdminAccountRequiredError` (HTTP 418, `.status_code`), `RateLimitError` (HTTP
  429 after retries, `.status_code`), `PeekGraphQLError` (`.graphql_errors` holds
  the raw list — a resolver-level failure), `PeekHttpError` (a non-2xx status
  other than 418/429 with no GraphQL `errors` — e.g. 401/404/5xx; carries
  `.status_code`, `.url`, and raw `.body`; a non-JSON error page keeps its
  status), `PiiAccessDisabledError` (a payment/booking-modification op was
  called without `full_customer_access`; `.operation`), the REST-sibling
  `CngApiError` / `AcmeApiError` (`.status_code`, `.body`), and
  `CngPermissionError` (CNG HTTP 403; `.permissions`, `.status_code`, raw
  `.body`) — all importable; branch with `except`.
- Token verification (`verify_peek_auth_token`, `parse_install_webhook`) raises
  PyJWT's `jwt.InvalidTokenError` subclasses (`ExpiredSignatureError`,
  `InvalidSignatureError`, `InvalidIssuerError`, `InvalidAudienceError`,
  `DecodeError`, …). Claim extraction never raises once the signature verifies:
  a missing `user` block gives `user=None`, and each user field (including
  `id`, the person's own id — not an account/partner id) is nullable, with
  `""`/`"null"` normalized to `None`.
- `ValueError` for validation/precondition failures raised before any request.

## Logging

`Logger` is a protocol with `info(message, context=None)` / `warn(...)` /
`error(...)`. Default is `noop_logger` (silent). `logging_adapter(logging_logger)`
wraps a standard-library `logging.Logger`, forwarding the context mapping as
`extra={"context": {...}}`.

## Webhooks (booking + waiver + install)

Two pure-transform parsers plus one verify-and-parse call. The pure parsers need
no auth/network/`PeekAccessService`; accept the `{<key>: …}` envelope, a bare
node, or a JSON string; never raise on malformed input. Registration is done
**once in an external system** (App Store config), not from code.

- `parse_booking_webhook(body) -> Booking` — auto-detects guests/breakdown.
  Booking payload shape is defined by a GraphQL selection registered externally;
  paste the canonical maximal selection into `output_fields_gql_query`. That
  string is documented in `docs/webhooks.md` and pinned by a drift-guard test —
  it is NOT a runtime export.
- `parse_waiver_webhook(body, options=None) -> Waiver` — maps the fixed
  `snake_case` `waiver_webhook_data` payload to the clean `Waiver` model. **No
  query to register** — just subscribe to the `agreement_signature_created`
  event. Takes the same `AccessOptions`; by default (`full_customer_access` off)
  `guest_name` is `None` and `file_url` is `""` — pass
  `AccessOptions(full_customer_access=True)` to keep them.
- `parse_install_webhook(token, body, secret) -> InstallWebhook` — the install
  webhook delivers **two payloads at once**: a signed `app_registry_v2` JWT and a
  JSON body. This **verifies** the token (HMAC signature + expiry +
  `app_registry_v2` issuer + `Joken` audience — same checks as
  `verify_peek_auth_token`, raising the underlying PyJWT error on failure, one
  `except jwt.InvalidTokenError` → `401`) and merges both into one flat,
  JSON-safe `InstallWebhook`: `install_id`, `account_id` (**also called the
  partner ID**), `account_name`, `platform`, `is_test`, `timezone`, `api_url`,
  `status`, `raw_status`, `display_version`, `user` (nullable, for
  system-initiated events). The **JSON body is the source of the event data**;
  the fields it shares with the token (`install_id`/`account_id`/`status`/
  `display_version`/`user`) fall back to the **verified token** when the body
  omits them. The token authenticates the whole delivery, so the body is
  trusted within a verified request. This webhook is the **only** source of
  `account_id`, `timezone`, and `api_url` in the package — no API read returns
  them; **persist them per install**. `status` and `platform` are **nullable**:
  a value this version does not recognise maps to `None` (wire value kept on
  `raw_status`) rather than being coerced, because Peek does not redeliver a
  2xx and a coerced status silently drops a lifecycle transition. Give both a
  fall-through branch that fails loudly. `token` is Peek's `x-peek-auth`
  request header value — pass it as-is, a `Bearer ` prefix is stripped for you.
  `secret` is the app's `jwt_secret`, app-wide, so it verifies fine on a
  brand-new install before any record exists. No query to register; just
  subscribe to the event.
  - The TypeScript package's deprecated `verifyInstallWebhook` was **not
    ported**; `parse_install_webhook` is the only install-webhook entry point.

**Full guide + booking query-to-register: `docs/webhooks.md` (shipped).**

## Notes for consumers

- Install from PyPI: `pip install peek-app-utilities` / `uv add peek-app-utilities`.
  See README "Install".
- Public entry point: the package root `peek_app_utilities`. Everything under
  `peek_app_utilities.internal` is internal — rely on the root barrel (and the
  documented `peek_app_utilities.models.peek.pricing` variant classes), don't
  deep-import internal modules.
- Not ported from `@peektravel/app-utilities`: the deprecated top-level
  short-form proxies on the access services (use `get_<resource>_service()`),
  `verifyInstallWebhook`, and the browser UI components (`/ui`).
